mentions.title: WARNING about King Main Thrust Bearings
mentions.snippet: Explicit buyer-warning thread about King main thrust bearings. Search results describe a King main bearing found out of spec on the free spread spec, and a later one also reported bad, raising the question of a manufacturing process problem. Thread was still active in June 2026.
mentions.replyNote: Readable today for the first time after months of 403s: no King or official reply, thread still open and unresolved, last post dated 3 June 2026.

mentions.title: King Main Bearings Defective
mentions.snippet: Poster reports King STDX thrust bearings measuring over 1mm too narrow to fit the block, and says the same issue was found across multiple BMW S65 and S85 blocks. A dimensional defect claim, not an install error.
mentions.replyNote: Still 307-redirects to the tollbit.m5board.com mirror instead of returning thread content; redirect not followed.

mentions.title: Just call it what it is---King Bearings are no longer an option....
mentions.snippet: Thread title is an outright recommendation against King. Results reference long-running back-order and availability problems on 6-bolt King bearings alongside quality-control concerns.
mentions.replyNote: Still returns HTTP 403 Forbidden; thread content could not be read.

mentions.title: King Bearing Failures?

mentions.title: King Bearings?
mentions.snippet: Long-running builder discussion of King bearings that mixes positive reports with criticism, including comments that King bearings run fat when hot and need extra cold clearance in steel rod and iron block builds.
mentions.replyNote: Thread read successfully; still no King or official brand representative reply and it remains open and unresolved.

mentions.title: No more King XP bearings
mentions.snippet: Thread about King XP bearings no longer being available; results attached to this search also mention bearing delamination in some high-performance applications. A King representative has already replied in this thread.
mentions.replyNote: Re-confirmed after last run's timeout: an official King Bearings representative replied near the end of the thread, noting it was an older thread recently brought to their attention and offering to investigate the specific bearings if details were provided.
